dof-copy-profile-final-cpu.json.limits: DOF index construction only. Synthetic repeated conformers from two corrected real-chemistry fixtures; both baseline and candidate pass named-atom and offset oracles. Five alternating rounds of five samples. Exact index/order equality. First device-table construction excluded; the shared KFO tensor aliases the existing chi-correction table. Peak is additional allocated CUDA tensor memory above inputs, not reserved/process memory. Excludes setup, actual sampling, DOF transfer and scoring; no whole-packer speed claim.

scheduler_changes: Job250036 initially queued in hpc-mid, whose start estimate was several days. It was changed to hpc-high, then shortened from1h to30min and routed to hpc-low to use spare H200 capacity on the extra interactive node. GPU/CPU/memory request stayed1GPU/4CPU/32GiB. No other jobs were modified. Final accounting records the actual allocation; partition-change metadata is retained.
limits: The production optimization preserves the original index/order outputs for valid compared inputs. Intermediate failures after enabling the source assertion are fixture errors, not evidence that the old copy kernel produced wrong offsets for valid tasks.

Both corrected fixtures pass the exact preceding implementation and the new implementation before final benchmarking. Initial prototypes used the older fixture mappings and must not be mixed with final profiles.
First device-table construction is excluded from latency; the same KFO tensor is shared with existing chi correction, with66,240B for the default PBT.

CUDA peak is additional allocated tensor memory, including outputs/temporaries, above prepared inputs. It excludes allocator reservations, Python metadata, source coordinates and total process memory.
Synthetic repeated states isolate index construction; they do not establish whole-packer speedups, DOF transfer bandwidth or arbitrary chemistry/parameter validity.
The first prototype was faster but used more memory at large sizes; later versions reuse freshly gathered buffers and release dead arrays sooner.
Runs overlap and must not be summed as unique coverage.
